lessons.title: The Greeks arrive
lessons.check_note: Yoma 69a, Avot 1:2 (Mishnah Yomit), Megillah 9a-b read on Sefaria 11/14. Dates, Josephus's parallel, the gymnasium (2 Maccabees 4) and Septuagint dating are from memory: check.

cards.title: A new world power
cards.body: In **332 BCE**, Alexander of Macedon sweeps through the Persian empire. Judea, a small temple-state around Jerusalem, now lives in a **Greek** world.

cards.q: In the Talmud's story, what did Alexander do when he met the High Priest Shimon HaTzaddik?
choices: Got down from his chariot and bowed to him

cards.title: The king bows
cards.body: The Samaritans won Alexander's permission to destroy the Temple. **Shimon HaTzaddik** put on the high priest's garments and walked all night, with Jerusalem's leaders carrying torches. At dawn the two camps met. Alexander **got down from his chariot and bowed**. Asked why, he said this man's face went before him to victory in every battle. Josephus tells a similar story; most historians doubt it happened.

cards.q: In Yoma 69a, why does Alexander bow to Shimon HaTzaddik?
choices: He had seen his face going before him to victory
He was afraid of the Jewish army
cards.why: The story makes the **priest**, not the conqueror, the greater power.

cards.title: Three things
cards.body: The Mishnah remembers the same Shimon as a teacher: "the world stands upon three things": the **Torah**, the **Temple service**, and **acts of piety**.
**Alexander** takes the land; after his death his generals split the empire.
The **Ptolemies** of Egypt rule Judea. Alexandria becomes a great Jewish city.
The **Seleucids** of Syria take Judea from Egypt.

cards.title: Becoming Greek
cards.body: Greek was now the language of trade, law and learning. Jews took Greek names: **Jason**, **Alexander**. In Jerusalem some built a **gymnasium**; others saw Greek ways as a threat to the covenant. That split will matter in the next lesson.

cards.title: Seventy-two elders
cards.body: King **Ptolemy** gathered seventy-two elders, put each in a separate room, and told each to translate the Torah. God put wisdom in every heart, and **all seventy-two wrote the same**. Scholars call this Greek Torah the **Septuagint**, made in Alexandria in the 3rd century BCE for Jews who no longer read Hebrew.

src.ref: Megillah 9a; scholars: Letter of Aristeas, Septuagint

cards.q: Who, in tradition, translated the Torah into Greek?
choices: Seventy-two elders, each in a separate room
wrong_why: Ezra is linked to the square script, not Greek.

src.ref: Megillah 9a; scholars: Letter of Aristeas, Septuagint

cards.gloss: "May God enlarge Japheth, And let him dwell in the tents of Shem" (9:27). Greece descends from Japheth, through Javan.

cards.title: Japheth's beauty
cards.body: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel allows a Torah scroll in **Greek**. His proof is this verse: Greek, the language of Japheth's son Javan, may live **in the tents of Shem**, where Torah is studied.

choices: To allow Torah in Greek, Japheth's language, in Shem's tents
cards.why: A **welcome**, within limits, to Greek culture.

cards.body: Next comes the clash with Greek rule that Hanukkah remembers. Its stories are in the Hanukkah unit.

cards.prompt: Jews have always borrowed from the cultures around them. What from your own world has deepened your Judaism?

points: **332 BCE**: Alexander; Judea in a Greek world.
Yoma 69a: the conqueror **bows** to the high priest.
Avot 1:2: Torah, Temple service, **acts of piety**.
Megillah 9a: **seventy-two elders**, one translation.
Megillah 9b: Japheth's language **in Shem's tents**.

lessons.title: The Hasmonean kings
lessons.check_note: 1 Maccabees 14 (Brenton), Kiddushin 66a read on Sefaria 11/14. Dates, the three parties (Josephus) and the scholarly reading of why the rabbis stress the oil are from memory: check.

cards.title: From rebels to rulers
cards.body: The **Maccabees** won back the Temple in 164 BCE. Then Judah's brothers did something larger: they built a **Jewish state**, independent for the first time since Babylon.

cards.q: In 1 Maccabees 14, what did the people make Simon the Hasmonean?
choices: Governor and high priest, until a faithful prophet arose
cards.why: Ruler and high priest, **with a condition**.

cards.body: The **revolt**; the Temple rededicated: Hanukkah.
**Simon** becomes high priest and ruler: the Hasmonean state.
**Alexander Yannai**, king and high priest, conquers widely.
Rome's general **Pompey** takes Jerusalem. Independence ends.

cards.title: Until a faithful prophet
cards.body: The Jews and priests agreed that Simon would be their "governor and high priest for ever, until there should arise a faithful prophet." The Hasmoneans were **priests**, not of David's line. The word **until** leaves room for God to say otherwise.

cards.q: Why does the decree for Simon say "until there should arise a faithful prophet"?
choices: His rule was not from David's line, so it stayed open to God's word
He was too young to rule
cards.why: A priestly ruler, **provisional** in the eyes of tradition.
wrong_why: Rome is a friend here, not a master.

cards.title: Three parties
cards.body: Under the Hasmoneans, Jews divided. **Pharisees**: teachers of the oral tradition, ancestors of the rabbis. **Sadducees**: the priestly elite, holding to the written Torah. **Essenes**: a strict, separate group; many scholars link them to the **Dead Sea Scrolls** at Qumran.

cards.title: The king and the sages
cards.body: King **Yannai** came home from conquering sixty cities and threw a feast for the sages. A troublemaker, Elazar ben Po'ira, turned him against them, and the sages were killed. The world was empty of Torah until **Shimon ben Shatach** "restored the Torah to its former glory."

cards.q: In Kiddushin 66a, who restored the Torah after Yannai killed the sages?
cards.why: The rabbis' hero here is a **sage**, not a king.

cards.title: Why the oil?
cards.body: The Talmud remembers Hanukkah by a **jar of oil**, not by battles, and reads Zechariah: "Not by might." Many scholars think the rabbis played down the Hasmonean kings after their rule turned harsh and later revolts failed. The **books of Maccabees** were not kept in the Jewish Bible.

cards.q: Why might the rabbis have stressed the oil over the Hasmonean victory?
choices: The Hasmonean kings had become harsh rulers
The oil story is in 1 Maccabees
wrong_why: The oil story is in the Talmud, not 1 Maccabees.

cards.body: The Hanukkah unit tells the story from the inside: the oil, the lights, and "Not by might."

cards.prompt: The Maccabees fought for freedom; their grandchildren ruled harshly. What helps a movement stay true to why it began?

points: **140 BCE**: Simon, ruler and high priest "**until... a faithful prophet**."
**Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes**.
Kiddushin 66a: Yannai and the sages; **Shimon ben Shatach**.
**63 BCE**: Rome. The rabbis remember the **oil**.

lessons.title: Herod and Rome
lessons.check_note: Bava Batra 3b-4a and Shabbat 31a read on Sefaria 11/14. Herod's dates, Idumean origin, the Western Wall and Hillel's dates are from memory: check.

cards.title: Rome's king
cards.body: In **37 BCE**, with Roman troops behind him, **Herod** takes Jerusalem. Rome's Senate has named him King of Judea.

cards.q: What does the Talmud say about Herod's rebuilt Temple?
choices: Whoever has not seen it has never seen a beautiful building

cards.body: **Herod** reigns as Rome's client king.
Herod begins **rebuilding the Temple** and its vast platform.
**Hillel** and **Shammai** teach in Jerusalem.

cards.title: A slave in the house
cards.body: The Talmud: "Herod was a slave in the house of the Hasmoneans." He killed his masters and took the throne, then killed the sages, sparing only **Bava ben Buta**, whom he blinded. Later Bava advised him to make amends by **rebuilding the Temple**. Historians: Herod was an **Idumean**, son of a Hasmonean official, and a brilliant, brutal ruler.

cards.q: In Bava Batra 3b, how did Herod come to rebuild the Temple?
choices: Bava ben Buta advised it as amends
cards.why: The Talmud turns a tyrant's project into **repentance**.

cards.title: The beautiful building
cards.body: The sages say whoever has not seen Herod's building "has never seen a beautiful building." Rows of white and green marble; he thought to cover it in gold and was told to leave it. The **Western Wall** is part of the retaining wall Herod built around the Temple Mount.

choices: Part of the retaining wall Herod built around the Temple Mount
The wall of the Holy of Holies
wrong_why: Solomon's Temple was gone by Herod's time.

cards.title: On one foot
cards.body: A non-Jew asked to learn the whole Torah standing on one foot. **Shammai** pushed him away with a builder's measuring stick. **Hillel** taught him: "That which is hateful to you do not do to another"; the rest is commentary, now go and learn it.

cards.gloss: "Love your fellow [Israelite] as yourself" (19:18). Hillel's rule says the same thing from the other side.

cards.q: How did Hillel answer the man who wanted the Torah on one foot?
choices: What is hateful to you, do not do to another; go and learn the rest
He told him to memorize the Ten Commandments
cards.why: A summary **and** an invitation to study.

cards.body: The houses of Hillel and Shammai argue all through the Mishnah, even about how to light Hanukkah candles.

cards.prompt: Herod built beauty and spilled blood; Hillel built a way of life with a sentence. Which kind of building lasts longer, and why?

points: **37 BCE**: Herod, Rome's king.
Bava Batra 3b: "**a slave in the house of the Hasmoneans**."
The **beautiful building**; the Western Wall.
Hillel: "**That which is hateful to you do not do to another**."

lessons.title: The Temple falls
lessons.check_note: Gittin 55b-56b and Avot D'Rabbi Natan 4:5 read on Sefaria 11/14. Gittin 56a's line on Rabbi Zekharya's humility, the coffin escape, dates, Masada, Arch of Titus and the Reform R'tzeh change are from memory: check.

cards.title: A feast and an insult
cards.body: The Talmud tells the fall of Jerusalem as a story about one party. A host sends for his friend **Kamtza**; the servant brings his enemy **Bar Kamtza** instead. The host throws him out, in front of the sages, who say nothing.

cards.q: What did Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai ask from the Roman general?

cards.body: Judea **revolts** against Rome.
Rome burns Jerusalem and the **Second Temple**: by tradition on the Ninth of Av.
**Masada**, the last fortress, falls.

cards.title: Silence at the feast
cards.body: "Jerusalem was destroyed on account of Kamtza and bar Kamtza." Shamed, Bar Kamtza tells Rome the Jews are rebelling, and sends a calf with a hidden blemish as the emperor's offering. **Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas** blocks both sacrificing it and killing the informer. Rome comes. The Talmud blames Zekharya's **excess humility**.

cards.q: In the Talmud's telling, what began the road to destruction?
choices: Public humiliation, and sages who stayed silent
cards.why: Not armies first, but **how people treated one another**.
wrong_why: The Talmud starts at the feast.

cards.title: Give me Yavne
cards.body: Rabban **Yochanan ben Zakkai** had his students carry him out of the besieged city in a coffin. Before the Roman general he asked: "Give me Yavne and its Sages," and doctors for a starving rabbi. Later voices asked why he did not ask to save **Jerusalem**. His answer became a new Judaism: of study, prayer and law.

cards.q: What did Yochanan ben Zakkai save?
wrong_why: The Talmud asks why he did not ask for it.

cards.title: Another atonement
cards.body: Leaving Jerusalem, Rabbi Yehoshua saw the ruins and cried: woe to us, the place where Israel's sins were atoned! Rabban Yochanan: do not grieve; we have another atonement as strong: "the practice of lovingkindness."

cards.gloss: "For I desire goodness, not sacrifice" (6:6), Yochanan ben Zakkai's proof.

cards.title: What Rome left
cards.body: In Rome, the **Arch of Titus** still shows soldiers carrying the Temple's **menorah**. Rome struck coins: **Judaea Capta**, Judea captured. The historian Josephus, a Jewish general who went over to Rome, saw it all.

src.ref: Arch of Titus; Judaea Capta coins; Josephus

cards.body: Prayer took the place of offerings. Reform siddurim also drop the plea to restore the sacrifices; check how R'tzeh reads in Mishkan T'filah.

cards.prompt: Yochanan ben Zakkai saved a school instead of a city. What would you carry out of a burning house, if not the house?

points: Gittin 55b: "**Jerusalem was destroyed on account of Kamtza and bar Kamtza**."
**70 CE**: the Second Temple falls.
"**Give me Yavne and its Sages**."
Kindness as atonement: "**I desire goodness, not sacrifice**."

lessons.title: Bar Kokhba
lessons.check_note: Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5 (Guggenheimer) and Berakhot 61b read on Sefaria 11/14. Dates, Aelia Capitolina, the Cave of Letters, and Akiva's last word 'echad' (61b, later in the passage) are from memory: check.

cards.title: A star from Jacob
cards.body: In **132 CE**, sixty years after the Temple fell, Judea rises against Rome again. Its leader is **Shimon bar Kosiba**, and the greatest sage of the age believes in him.

cards.q: What did Rabbi Akiva call Bar Kokhba?

cards.body: The **Bar Kokhba revolt**: for three years, a free Judea.
**Betar** falls. Jerusalem becomes a Roman city, **Aelia Capitolina**, closed to Jews.

cards.gloss: "A star rises from Jacob" (24:17). Kokhav, star, becomes his nickname: **Bar Kokhba**, son of a star.

cards.title: Star or liar?
cards.body: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Akiva taught that "a star out of Jacob" meant **Koziba**, and seeing him said, this is the King Messiah. **Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta** answered: "Grass will grow from your jaws," and David's son still will not have come. Later the rabbis called him **Bar Koziba**, son of a lie.

cards.q: How did Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta answer Akiva?
choices: You will be long dead before the Messiah comes
You are right; he is the Messiah

cards.title: His own letters
cards.body: In **1960-61**, in caves near the Dead Sea, archaeologists found letters signed by **Shimon bar Kosiba** himself, giving orders to his commanders. One asks that the **four species** be brought for Sukkot.

cards.q: What did the Cave of Letters reveal?
choices: Letters from Bar Kokhba himself, under his real name
A Roman account of his victory

cards.title: With all your soul
cards.body: After the revolt, Rome banned teaching Torah. Akiva taught anyway, and was executed. As they tore his flesh, he recited the Sh'ma. His students asked: even now? He said: "All my days I have been troubled by the verse: With all your soul." Now he could fulfill it. He died on the word **echad**, one.

cards.q: Why did Akiva say the Sh'ma as he died?
choices: He could finally love God "with all your soul"
It was the hour for evening prayer only
cards.why: His death became a teaching about **the Sh'ma**.
wrong_why: It was time for the Sh'ma, but that is not his reason.

cards.body: Each time you say the Sh'ma, "with all your soul" carries Akiva's story. On Tisha B'Av, Jews mourn Betar too.

cards.prompt: Akiva backed a leader who failed, and is still the rabbis' hero. What do you make of a great person's great mistake?

points: **132-135 CE**: Bar Kokhba's revolt; Betar falls.
Akiva: "**A star rises from Jacob**"; ben Torta: "**Grass will grow from your jaws**."
The **Cave of Letters**: Shimon bar Kosiba.
Berakhot 61b: Akiva and the Sh'ma, **with all your soul**.
